source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: In those{H1992} days{H3117} came{H935} Yochanan{H3110} the Immerser{H2881}, expounding{H1875} in the wilderness{H4057} of Yehudah{H3063},

one_way_hebrew: המטביל — from טבל (H2881), the Torah's own dipping verb (Lev 4:6; 14:6; and Naaman, who 'dipped — ויטבל — in the Jordan,' 2 Kgs 5:14): 'Yochanan the Immerser' names a Torah practice by its Torah verb. Greek βαπτιστής is built on a Greek verb and hides the continuity.
דורש (H1875) — 'expounding': the darash of scripture-exposition (whence midrash), as at 24:14. Greek κηρύσσων ('heralding') flattens the teacher into a crier.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ששי (Perek 6) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (3:1): יהודה] יודא BCDEFG.

verses.translation: and saying{H559}: Turn back in repentance{H8666}, for the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} is near{H7138} to come.

one_way_hebrew: חזרו בתשובה — 'return in teshuvah': the rabbinic idiom for repentance itself (חזרה בתשובה), built on the prophets' שובו (Hos 14:2-3, שובה ישראל). Greek μετανοεῖτε ('change your mind') is a different anthropology — the Greek repents in his thinking, the Hebrew turns around and comes home.

מלכות שמים — 'the kingdom of Heaven': the rabbinic reverent idiom (as in קבלת עול מלכות שמים). Greek Matthew's ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν is a calque of exactly this Hebrew phrase — Mark and Luke, writing for gentiles, translate it away ('kingdom of God'). The phrase is native here and borrowed there.

verses.translation: to establish{H6965} what was said{H559} by Yeshayahu{H3470} the prophet{H5030}: A voice{H6963} cries{H7121} in the wilderness{H4057}: Prepare{H6437} the way{H1870} of YHWH{H3068}, make straight{H3474} in the desert plain{H6160} a highway{H4546} for our Elohim{H430}.

one_way_hebrew: The whole of Isa 40:3 in Isaiah's own words — including the half Greek Matthew does not carry: ישרו בערבה מסילה לאלקינו ('make straight in the ARAVAH a HIGHWAY for OUR GOD'). Greek Matthew quotes the LXX's short form and changes 'the paths of our God' to 'his paths'; this text keeps ערבה (H6160), מסילה (H4546), and לאלקינו intact — the one whose way Yochanan prepares is YHWH, named twice, in Isaiah's own parallel clauses. A back-translator from Greek Matthew could not have recovered the missing half-verse.
textual_notes: The ms writes ע״י (the scribal abbreviation of על ידי, 'by the hand of') and ה״ for the Name — first occurrences in this chapter (see 1:22).
Howard's apparatus (3:3): ישרו . . . לאלקינו omitted in G; הנביא omitted in ABEFG.

verses.translation: And behold{H2009}, Yochanan{H3110} was clothed{H3847} with camel's{H1581} wool{H6785}, and black{H7838} leather{H5785} girded{H232} his loins{H4975}; and his food{H4203} was the locust{H697} and the honey{H1706} of the forests{H3293}.

one_way_hebrew: אזור... במתניו — Eliyahu's uniform, verbatim: ואזור עור אזור במתניו ('and a girdle of leather girded about his loins,' 2 Kgs 1:8) — the sentence by which Ahaziah recognized Elijah. The Hebrew dresses Yochanan in Elijah's own verse.

ודבש היערים — 'honey of the FORESTS': יערת הדבש of 1 Sam 14:25-27 (Jonathan's honeycomb in the wood; יער carries the honey-sense in its own right). Greek μέλι ἄγριον ('wild honey') keeps the fact and loses the scripture.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew specifies 'BLACK leather' (עור שחור) and camel's WOOL (צמר); Greek has plain 'leather girdle' and camel's 'HAIR' (τρίχας).
textual_notes: The transcription reads ויערים; the scan reads היערים, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (3:4): לבוש] + מלבוש ABDG; והנה יוחנן] והיה יוחנן EF; אזור] ואזור ABDEF, + על בשרו G.

verses.translation: Then{H227} they went out{H3318} to him from Yerushalayim{H3389} and from all{H3605} Yehudah{H3063} and from all the kingdom{H4438} around{H5439} the Jordan{H3383},

greek_deviations: 'All the KINGDOM (המלכות) around the Jordan' — Greek has περίχωρος, 'the region.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (3:5): המלכות] הממלכות A, מלכות FG; מירושלם ומכל יהודה] מיהודה ומירושלם EF; יהודה] יודא BDG.

verses.translation: and then were confessing{H3034} their sin{H2403} and immersing{H2881} in the Jordan{H3383} at his word{H3982}.

one_way_hebrew: מתודים (H3034, hitpael) — the Torah's confession verb: והתודו את חטאתם ('they shall confess their sin,' Num 5:7; Lev 5:5; 16:21 — the Yom Kippur confession). The Hebrew describes vidui-and-tevilah — confession and immersion, the Torah's own repentance sequence.

וטובלים — in the Hebrew the people immerse (active, as at every mikveh); Greek ἐβαπτίζοντο ὑπ' αὐτοῦ makes John the operator. על מאמרו — 'at his WORD' (מאמר, H3982, Esth 1:15; 9:32): they act on his ma'amar; the clause has no Greek counterpart.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק שביעי (Perek 7) begins at v. 7.
Howard's apparatus (3:6): ואז omitted in ABDEFG; מתודים] ומתודים G; על] + פי B.

verses.translation: And he saw{H7200} that many{H7227} of the Perushim{H6567} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, Farisei — and of the Perushim came{H935} to his immersion{H2881}, and he told{H559} them to flee{H1272} from the wrath{H7110} destined{H6264} to come{H935} from El{H410}.

one_way_hebrew: קצף (H7110) — the Bible's own wrath-noun: כי יצא הקצף ('wrath has gone out,' Num 17:11); Isa 54:8. With לעתיד לבא — 'destined to come' — the same idiom of appointed future as 24:6 (עתיד לבא). Greek ὀργὴ μέλλουσα translates both halves.
The scribe glosses the Hebrew פרושים with the church's word — בלעז פאריזיאי — as with קריס״טוס (1:16) and מי״רא (2:11): the Greek-Latin vocabulary is the visitor being explained, not the source.
greek_deviations: NO 'BROOD OF VIPERS' in the base text: Yochanan simply 'told them to flee from the wrath to come.' The other mss supply an address in two independent forms — A: זרע תנינים מי למד לכם ('offspring of serpents, who taught you'); DG (EF similarly): שרש פתנים מי הורה לכם ('root of adders' — פתן, Isa 11:8's adder — 'who instructed you'). Howard prints '(Offspring of serpents, who taught you)' in parentheses. Divergent supplements again mark the short base as prior.
The base repeats הפרושים twice where Greek has 'Pharisees and Sadducees'; mss ABDEFG correct the second to הצדיקים. Howard prints '(Sadducees).'
translation_notes: The transcription reads הפצף; the scan reads הקצף, corrected here. The printed פאריזיאי carries vowel points; stripped here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (3:7): הפרושים (2nd)] הצדיקים ABDEFG; פאריזיאי] פארישיאוש ADEFG; בלעז] לעז ADEFG; להם] אלהם זרע תנינים מי למד לכם A, אלהם שרש פתנים מי הורה לכם DG; לעתיד] העתיד ABDEFG; מהאל] מן האל G.

verses.translation: Produce{H6213} the fruit{H6529} of complete{H8003} repentance{H8666}.

one_way_hebrew: תשובה שלמה — 'complete repentance': the fixed Hebrew term (teshuvah shelemah) of the liturgy and the rabbis, standing here as a natural construct phrase. Greek καρπὸν ἄξιον τῆς μετανοίας ('fruit worthy of repentance') paraphrases an idiom Greek does not have.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (3:8): השלמה] שלמה DG.

verses.translation: And do not say{H559} in your hearts{H3824}: Avraham{H85} is our father{H1}. Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you that Elohim{H430} is able{H3201} to raise up{H6965} his son{H1121} Avraham from these{H428} stones{H68}.

one_way_hebrew: The saying turns on a pun that exists only in Hebrew: אבנים and בנים — stones and sons share their consonants (the בן inside every אבן). Greek λίθων/τέκνα has no echo at all. Behind it stands Isa 51:1-2: 'look to the ROCK from which you were hewn... look to Avraham your father' — stones, quarry, and Abraham already joined in Isaiah.
greek_deviations: The base reads 'to raise up HIS SON AVRAHAM from these stones' (את בנו אברהם) — against the boast 'Avraham is our father,' God can quarry Avraham himself anew; Greek reads 'to raise up children to Abraham.' Howard translates the base as it stands ('his son Abraham').
translation_notes: אמן and את — the transcription reads אמנ and עת; the scan reads אמן and את, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (3:9): אלקים] האלקים A, האלהים BDEFG.

verses.translation: (And already the axe{H1631} has reached{H5060} the root{H8328} of the tree{H6086}; that which does not produce{H6213} good{H2896} fruit{H6529} will be cut down{H3772} and burned{H8313} in fire{H784}. And the companies{H2274} asked{H7592} him: If so, what shall we do{H6213}? And Yochanan{H3110} answered{H6030} them: Whoever has{H3426} two{H8147} tunics{H3801}, let him give{H5414} the one to him who has none{H369}. And the people{H5971} came{H935} to be immersed{H2881}.) And many{H7227} asked him{H7592}: What shall we do? And he answered{H6030} them: Be grieved for no man{H376}, and do not punish them{H6064}, and be glad{H8055} with your portion{H2506}. And all{H3605} the people{H5971} were thinking{H2803} and reckoning{H1819} in their circumcised{H4135} heart{H3820}: Yochanan — he is Yeshua{H3442}.

one_way_hebrew: כתנות — the kethoneth again (Gen 3:21; 37:3; see 5:40; 24:18); Luke's χιτῶνας translates it. חלק — 'be glad in your PORTION' (חלק, Eccl 5:18, ולשמח... זה מתת אלהים; Ps 16:5) — the counsel is Qohelet's own vocabulary.
greek_deviations: THIS VERSE IS LUKE INSIDE MATTHEW: the crowds' question 'what shall we do?', the two tunics, the counsel against extortion, contentment with one's portion, and the people's musing about John are Luke 3:10-15 — standing here in the Hebrew Matthew where Greek Matthew has only the axe-saying. The Shem Tov text carries a fuller Baptist tradition; and where Luke 3:15 has the people wonder 'whether he were the Messiah,' this text has them wonder whether Yochanan IS Yeshua (mss ABDEFG: אם באולי יוחנן הוא ישו, 'whether perhaps Yochanan was Yeshu').
translation_notes: תצטערו לשום איש ולא תענשום — compressed counsel ('be grieved for no man, and do not fine/punish them'), answering Luke 3:14's charge to the soldiers ('do violence to no man... be content with your wages'); Howard renders 'Be anxious for (no) man and do not chastise them.' צער is the rabbinic grief-word; ענש (H6064) is the Torah's fine-word (Exod 21:22; Deut 22:19).
בלבם נמול — 'in their CIRCUMCISED heart' (Howard's construal); mss ABDEF omit נמול. Deut 30:6's circumcised heart stands behind the phrase.
textual_notes: THE PARENTHESIZED SECTION (from וכבר through להטביל) IS MISSING FROM THE BASE MS: Howard's apparatus (3:10): 'וכבר . . . להטביל] omit Brit. Lib. ms & C, Text = ABDEFG' — he supplies it from ABDEFG and prints it in parentheses. The base ms of Matt 3:10 begins at וישאלוהו רבים.
Howard's apparatus (3:10) further: נמול omitted in ABDEF; יוחנן . . . ישו] אם באולי יוחנן הוא ישו ABDEFG.
Transcription corrections per scan: וישאלו (for וישאל), הא׳ (the scan's abbreviation of האחד, 'the one'; scrambled in the transcription), הוא (for הו).

verses.translation: And Yochanan{H3110} answered{H6030} them all{H3605}: In truth{H571}, behold{H2009}, I immerse{H2881} you in the days{H3117} of repentance{H8666}; but after{H310} me comes{H935} one mightier{H2389} than I — whose sandal{H5275}-thong{H8288} I am not worthy to loosen{H5425} — and he will immerse you with the fire{H784} of the Spirit{H7307} of Holiness{H6944}.

one_way_hebrew: שרוך נעלו — Gen 14:23's exact pair: מחוט ועד שרוך נעל ('from a thread to a sandal-thong'), Avram's oath-word for the least valuable thing there is. 'Not worthy to loosen his sandal-thong' reaches for the Torah's own idiom of the negligible; Greek ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων translates the object and loses the oath. להתיר — the loosing verb of Ps 105:20 (ויתירהו, Joseph loosed from prison).
greek_deviations: Three readings against the Greek: (1) בימי תשובה — 'in the DAYS of repentance' (mss DEF read במי, 'with the WATERS of repentance'; Greek: 'with water unto repentance') — the base makes John's immersion belong to a season, not a substance; (2) באש רוח הקדוש — 'with the FIRE OF the Spirit of Holiness': one baptism, not two ('with the Holy Spirit and with fire'); (3) ענה לכולם — 'he answered them ALL,' agreeing with Luke 3:16 (ἀπεκρίνατο... πᾶσιν) against Greek Matthew, which has no such audience marker.
translation_notes: אתכם — the transcription reads עתכם; scan corrected.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (3:11): בימי] במי DEF; ענה] אמר EF.

verses.translation: whose winnowing fork{H4214} is in his hand{H3027} to winnow{H2219} his threshing floor{H1637}, and he will gather{H622} the grain{H1715} into his storehouse{H214}, and the straw{H8401} — and so on.

one_way_hebrew: מזרה (H4214) — the prophets' winnowing fork: ואזרם במזרה בשערי הארץ ('I will winnow them with a winnowing fork in the gates of the land,' Jer 15:7; cf. Isa 30:24). The whole scene — זרה, גרן, דגן, תבן — is the harvest-judgment vocabulary of the prophets, native words all.
textual_notes: The verse ends והתבן ע״כ — 'and the straw, thus far' (עד כאן): the scribe breaks off exactly as he broke off Jer 31:15 with וכו׳ (2:18) — the ending was too well known to copy. Mss ABDEFG complete it: ישרוף באש אשר לא תכבה ('he will burn with fire which shall not be quenched' — the לא תכבה of Isa 66:24), and Howard prints the completion in parentheses.
Howard's apparatus (3:12): והתבן] + ישרוף באש אשר לא תכבה ABDEFG; בידו] ביד D.

verses.translation: Then{H227} came{H935} Yeshua{H3442} from the Galil{H1551} to the Jordan{H3383}, to be immersed{H2881} by Yochanan{H3110}.

translation_notes: להטביל מיוחנן — 'to be immersed FROM Yochanan': the active form carries the passive sense (so also v. 14, להטביל מידך); mss EF read the nifal להטבל.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק שמיני (Perek 8) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (3:13): את] אל B.

verses.translation: And Yochanan{H3110} was in doubt about immersing him{H2881}, and said{H559}: I ought to be immersed{H2881} from your hand{H3027} — and you come{H935} to me{H413}?

one_way_hebrew: מספק — safeq, the rabbinic term for halakhic doubt: 'Yochanan was in doubt' is a native Hebrew writer's sentence. Greek διεκώλυεν ('was preventing him') is a different and stronger act; the Hebrew gives the hesitation of a man weighing a ruling.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (3:14): מידך] על ידיך A; להטביל] להטבל EF.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} and said{H559} to him: Permit it{H3240}, for thus we{H587} are obligated to complete{H7999} all{H3605} righteousness{H6666}. And then{H227} they immersed him{H2881}.

one_way_hebrew: חייבים — chayav, the Mishnah's constant word for legal obligation: 'we are OBLIGATED to complete all righteousness' is halakhic Hebrew — duty, not decorum. Greek πρέπον ἐστίν ('it is fitting') is aesthetic where the Hebrew is legal. And להשלים — 'to complete, make whole' — is the same verb the Torah-saying of 5:17 turns on (לא... להפר... אלא להשלים): the immersion and the Torah stand under one verb of completion.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (3:15): לו] אליו ABDEFG; הטבילוהו] הטבילהו ADEFG, + יוחנן BC — Howard's English: 'then (John baptized him).'

verses.translation: And immediately, when he came up{H5927} from the water{H4325}, the heavens{H8064} were opened{H6605} to him, and he saw{H7200} the Spirit{H7307} of Elohim{H430} descending{H3381} like a dove{H3123}, and it rested upon him{H5921}.

one_way_hebrew: רוח אלקים over the water — Gen 1:2's exact pair (ורוח אלהים מרחפת על פני המים): at the Jordan the creation scene recurs, the Spirit of Elohim over the waters, hovering bird-like (the rabbis themselves read מרחפת 'like a dove that hovers over her young,' b. Chagigah 15a). Greek πνεῦμα θεοῦ translates the phrase and loses the scene.

ושרתה עליו — 'and it RESTED upon him': the idiom of the Shekhinah's resting (שרתה שכינה) and of Isa 11:2, ונחה עליו רוח יהוה ('the Spirit of YHWH shall rest upon him') — the Branch of Yishai again (see 2:23). The Hebrew says of Yeshua what Isaiah says of the Branch.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (3:16): שעלה] עלה EF; וירא] + דמות G ('the likeness of'); אלקים] אלים A.

verses.translation: And behold{H2009}, a voice{H6963} from the heavens{H8064} saying{H559}: This is my son{H1121}, my beloved{H157} — exceedingly{H3966}, exceedingly loved{H157} — and my delight{H2656} is in him.

one_way_hebrew: בני אהובי — the Akedah's phrase-world: בנך יחידך אשר אהבת ('your son, your only one, whom you love,' Gen 22:2); and the doubled מאד מאד is Hebrew's own superlative (Gen 17:2,6 במאד מאד). Greek ὁ ἀγαπητός flattens the triple love-phrase (אהובי... נאהב) into one adjective.

וחפצי בו — 'my DELIGHT is in him': the chefets of Isa 62:4 (חפצי־בה, 'My-delight-is-in-her') and the servant of Isa 42:1 in whom the soul delights; Greek ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα translates the idiom. The bat-kol speaks Isaiah's vocabulary in Hebrew.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (3:17): מן השמים] מהשמים ABDEFG; נאהב] מאהב G.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 3 in the Shem Tov Hebrew reads as a Hebrew Baptist-narrative with Luke's fuller material inside it. (1) 3:3 quotes the WHOLE of Isa 40:3 — including ישרו בערבה מסילה לאלקינו ('a highway for OUR GOD'), the half-verse Greek Matthew lacks: the way John prepares is YHWH's, twice named. (2) 3:10 carries Luke 3:10-15 — the crowds' 'what shall we do?', the two tunics, contentment with one's portion, and the people wondering about John — inside Matthew; its first half is missing from the base ms and supplied from ABDEFG (Howard prints it in parentheses), and the musing runs 'Yochanan — is he Yeshua?'. (3) The base text has NO 'brood of vipers' (3:7): the other mss supply it in two competing forms (A 'offspring of serpents'; DG 'root of adders'). (4) 3:11: 'I immerse you in the DAYS of repentance' (DEF: 'waters'); 'he will immerse you with the FIRE OF the Spirit of Holiness' — one baptism; 'answered them ALL' agrees with Luke 3:16. (5) The proclamation is rabbinic Hebrew: חזרו בתשובה ('return in teshuvah'), מלכות שמים — the very phrase Greek Matthew calques; פרי תשובה השלמה (3:8). (6) One-way idioms: המטביל from the Torah's טבל; Elijah's girdle verbatim (2 Kgs 1:8) with 'BLACK leather' (3:4); confession vidui-style (Num 5:7) 'at his word' (3:6); שרוך נעלו = Gen 14:23; the stones/sons pun אבנים/בנים with the base reading 'raise up HIS SON Avraham' (3:9); Gen 1:2's רוח אלקים over the water with Isa 11:2's resting (3:16); the Akedah's beloved son and Isa 62:4's חפצי (3:17). (7) 3:12 ends 'and the straw — עד כאן': the scribe abbreviates the known ending (mss complete with Isa 66:24's 'fire not quenched'), the same Hebrew-audience fingerprint as 2:18's וכו׳. Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 6), 7 (Perek 7), and 13 (Perek 8).
